title: Blue September kicks off 2015 campaign revealing their new research on men's attitudes to their health
introduction:
Blue September sponsored by Vhi Healthcare returns this September 2015 to generate awareness about male specific cancers. This year the campaign aims to highlight men’s attitudes to their health and wants to encourage men to be more proactive about checking themselves for signs of cancer.

To kick off this year’s campaign, the Men’s Cancer Alliance (the charities behind Blue September), in collaboration with Behaviour & Attitudes Research, conducted a survey of over 900 Irish men covering a broad demographic profile, investigating their knowledge of male specific cancers, as well as their habits and attitudes towards their health. The findings highlight how little Irish men know about male specific cancers and the symptoms they should look out for.
keyPoints:
• Almost half of men researched in the risk age category for testicular cancer would not be confident in recognizing the common symptoms of testicular cancer.
  • 80% of the men researched in the risk age category for testicular cancer did not know that the best way to check for testicular cancer symptoms is a regular self- check.
  • 81% of men aged 16 and over in Ireland have neither checked themselves or been checked by a doctor for a prostate or testes related problem.
  • 44% believed that the reason for men generally being slower to visit their doctor compared to women is because they are afraid of finding out what the problem is. This peaks at 54% amongst farmers. 41% of men also said that they would hope the symptoms would simply go away.
  • 24% of men researched felt that their reluctance to going to the doctor is down to being embarrassed; this peaks at 35% amongst 16-24year olds.
  • There is a general message that famers are not confident in recognising the common symptoms of testicular or prostate cancer.
body:
Micheal Sheridan of the Men’s Cancer Alliance & CEO Mercy Hospital Foundation commented : “This year’s research results demonstrate that the Blue September awareness campaign it vitally important. Our aim is to educate men about men’s cancers and teach them to be more symptom aware, as early detection significantly improves survival rates. At the Men’s Cancer Alliance we have produced a series of pocket sized fold out leaflets, each dedicated to specific cancers like penile, prostate, testicular and bowel, highlighting the symptoms of each cancer and in some cases how to check for them. These easy to read leaflets are available from Men’s Cancer Alliance website, menscancer.ie. We are asking the public to support this campaign by organising a fundraising event or by making a donation via www.blueseptember.ie”.

Dr. Bernadette Carr, Medical Director of Vhi Healthcare said: “Vhi Healthcare is delighted to partner with Blue September, a campaign which is helping to increase awareness about male specific cancers and is urging men to start facing up to cancer and be more proactive in looking after their health. Survival rates are increasing due to improved treatments and therapies. An early diagnosis improves your chances dramatically, so take the time to check yourself out and stay vigilant. Vhi continues to be to the forefront helping men to detect cancer in the early stages through screening at its Vhi Medical Centres based in Dublin and Cork. These centres provide customers with access to tests and screenings designed to check specifically for risk factors associated with diseases such as colon cancer and others.”

Blue September sponsored by Vhi Healthcare will continue the conversation generating awareness and discussion of men’s cancers and working to encourage men to look after their health for the month of September.
notesToEditors:
About Blue September:

Blue September is an international initiative first launched in New Zealand in 2008. Blue September has grown into an international campaign and over the past five years has seen phenomenal response amongst men in Ireland. Coordinated in Ireland by the Men’s Cancer Alliance (MCA) which includes the Mater Hospital Foundation, Mercy Hospital Foundation and Cancer Care West and is sponsored by Vhi Healthcare, the MCA are delighted to welcome back Vhi Healthcare for the third year for Blue September 2015.

About Men’s Cancer Alliance (MCA):

Men’s Cancer Alliance (MCA) is the umbrella alliance, formed by The Mater Hospital Foundation (Leinster), The Mercy Hospital Foundation (Munster) and Cancer Care West (West and North West) organisations. The aim of the Men’s Cancer Alliance is to create awareness about men’s cancers, treatments and supports available and to raise funds to create and maintain a number of men’s cancer support initiatives. The Mater Foundation, The Mercy Hospital Foundation and Cancer Care West are the three organisations behind the successful Blue September men’s cancers awareness campaign.

Blue September “Keepy Uppy” online and mobile app game:

The idea: play- keep up the ball - share your score - make a donation - then nominate a friend to do the same, creating a chain of awareness and donations nationwide. All proceeds will go towards fundraising for improved diagnostics; treatment and care for men with cancer. Log onto www.blueseptember.ie to play and donate.

Further information on Blue September sponsored by Vhi, can be accessed at www.blueseptember.ie
